narrative.overview:
The app is a researcher's notebook laid over a map. The map of hex cells is the page's subject and takes nearly all of it; the panels are the notes in its margin: plain, practical, written to be used, at a desk while exploring or on a phone while walking an area. A note says what a mark means and where it came from, and then gets out of the way. Every score can be traced, so the notes are full of small, exact words and never of slogans.

The panels are quiet and exact. Grey text, thin borders, white paper and system type: nothing in them competes with the map. Colour has two jobs only, and both carry meaning: the score scale on the map, the legend and every bar; and each top-level factor's own colour in the boxes, the rings and the swatches beside the sliders. Detail opens on demand, so the surface stays the answer and the notebook holds the working.

This is not an estate agent's site, and it is not a dashboard either.
keyCharacteristics: The map fills the window; the panels float over it at its edges, never beside it in a column of their own.
One score scale everywhere, and colour used only where it means something.
System sans-serif type in three sizes, with figures in tabular numerals.
Actions are underlined words, not buttons; the only filled control is the chosen side of a switch.
Flat paper, a hairline of shadow to lift a panel off the map, and nothing more.

rules.name: The Meaning Only Rule
rules.body: A colour in this app always means something: a score, a factor, the land, or a warning. Decoration in colour is not allowed; a new colour must name what it means.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Every score, anywhere, takes the same red → yellow → blue-green scale (web/src/features/map/colour.ts). Never a second scale, and never a factor colour for a score.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that sits in a column or changes as a slider moves (shares, scores, ranks) uses tabular numerals, so it does not jump.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Labels are plain words a newcomer understands; jargon stays in the code and the docs for contributors.

rules.name: The Margin Note Rule
rules.body: A panel is a note on the map, not a card on a page. One level of lift only: no card inside a card, and no shadow inside a panel.

dos: Do let the map fill the window and float the panels over its edges.
Do colour every score with the one scale in web/src/features/map/colour.ts, and show it as a length and a number too.
Do use the factor's own colour only to say which factor a thing belongs to.
Do write labels in plain words, help in label-sized quiet ink, and numbers in tabular numerals.
Do keep text at WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) or better, placeholders included, and targets on a phone at 44px or more.
Do put detail one step down: hover for a quick look, click for the reasons, "About the data" for the sources.
donts: Don't make it look like an estate agent's site: no photographs of houses, no big call-to-action buttons, no sales words.
Don't add dashboard clutter: no grid of cards, headline figures or charts that compete with the map.
Don't add a colour that means nothing, a second score scale, or a factor colour on a score.
Don't put a card inside a card or a shadow inside a panel.
Don't add a display typeface or a second font family.
Don't draw over the basemap's credits: they are a licence condition.
